paper: D. Marcuse, C. R. Menyuk, P. K. A. Wai, Application of the Manakov-PMD equation to studies of signal propagation in optical fibers with randomly varying birefringence, J. Lightwave Technol. 15, 1735 (1997)
description: Manakov/8-9 averaged equation and the random-birefringence equivalent: (i) the Manakov soliton width/power law Eq. (30) with the explicit 8/9, (ii) the Fig. 5 fluctuation of the random-birefringence soliton (~1%) around the Manakov solution, (iii) the Fig. 4 NRZ dispersion-map system (16-bit PRBS, lossless 500 km, reduced to 2 periods for runtime) propagated with the random SU(2) rotation engine vs the deterministic averaged Manakov run.

nrz.note_pattern: pseudorandom word; exact bit sequence not specified in the paper — a fixed pseudorandom word is recorded here and in reproduce.py

pmd.note: Sec. III example: dz=1 km, L_corr=100 m, Lambda_beat=50 m, D_PMD=3 ps/km^(1/2), delta z = Lambda_beat/30 = 1.67 m (paper Eq. (28): b = pi/Lambda_beat, nu' = D_PMD/(2 sqrt(2 L_corr)), sigma = sqrt(delta z/(2 L_corr)))

pmd_extreme_mixed_length.note: Sec. IV-C / Fig. 6: same Sec. IV-A parameter set with L_corr = 10 m and Lambda_beat = 10 km; to see a nonlinear-PMD effect the paper further lowered L_corr to 1 m. Only the stated geometry is recorded here; the nonlinear-PMD term is not implemented in the engine.

soliton_check.note: Eq. (30): tau_m = [9/(8(|U|^2+|V|^2)_peak)]^(1/2) in soliton units -> the Manakov fundamental soliton carries a peak SUM power 9/8 times the scalar-soliton peak for the same width.

grid.note: paper used 2^10 points for the NRZ runs (Fig. 4/5 soliton checks smaller window)

engine.birefringent_run: RandomBirefringenceEngine (random SU(2) frame rotations Eq. (34)/(35) class, uniform axis + uniform angle)
engine.note_rotation_step: the paper resolves delta z = Lambda_beat/30 = 1.67 m for its linear M-matrix evaluation; the nonlinear Fig. 5 run converges by delta_z_j ~ 20 m (peak fluctuation saturates at 2.3 % for steps <= 20 m; the paper's own CNLS-run value is ~1 %). Runtime ~5 s per 30-z0 run.
engine.note_nrz: Fig. 4 runs use a 100 m frame step — the Poincare-sphere mixing length Lambda_beat^2/(12 pi^2 L_corr) = 4.2 m is far shorter, so mixing is rapid; birefringent vs averaged-Manakov detected currents agree to 2e-4 relative L2 (the paper claims 'exactly the same output').
